The top 13 trending news stories in the universe, ranked every hour at the 13th minute UTC.
The flagship for news around the universe. Adults 21+. For entertainment purposes only.

## 2026-10-20 20:13 UTC
1. UN News | More than 250,000 people have now fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the UN said, with access to Taiz essentially blocked, sanitation halted by diesel shortages, World Food Programme wheat flour stocks nearly exhausted and 10 of 16 Taiz districts at emergency hunger levels — a mass displacement crisis deepening behind closed routes.
2. CNN | Experts warned in a letter shared with CNN that Trump administration cuts to the GeoXO weather satellite programme — two fewer satellites and three fewer instruments — could set US weather forecasting back by a decade, weakening the ability to understand weather, climate and the world.
3. DailyBrief | About 6,000 seafarers remain trapped in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Middle East war, International Maritime Organization head Arsenio Dominguez said in a Sunday interview, urging ships not to transit the strait due to continuing attacks on vessels — a chokepoint warning for global shipping and energy.
4. Axios | US Secretary Pete Hegseth met Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday amid discussions of a possible renewed military campaign against Iran, Axios reported, as a third US aircraft carrier is expected to arrive in the Middle East soon.
5. WSJ | Former Trump and Biden officials warned the US needs an energy push to win the economic race with China, the Wall Street Journal reported, as a Senate permitting bill would overhaul environmental rules, strengthen the grid and make data centers pay their full transmission costs — praised by oil, gas and renewables groups and opposed by 185 community, labour and climate organisations.
6. The Quantum Insider | Alice & Bob reported demonstrating every building block of a cat-qubit logical qubit in France's PROQCIMA programme — noise-biased CNOT gates, measure-and-reset, repeated distance-3 error-correction cycles and a first non-Clifford gate — with its digital twin showing the coherence gains still needed to operate below threshold.
7. Daily Graphic | Ghana's Petroleum Hub Development Corporation signed a $28 billion build-own-operate deal with a Korea-Emirati-Mali consortium led by Global Sphere for phase two of the Jomoro hub — a 300,000-barrel-per-day refinery, two petrochemical plants, four million cubic metres of storage and a multi-berth jetty, with construction expected to start in the first quarter of next year.
8. Daily Graphic | Ghana's President John Mahama told investors the country will phase out raw mineral exports by 2030 to force local processing and refining — a value-addition policy that would reshape how one of West Africa's major mining economies sells its resources.
9. Fox News | US consumer prices rose 3.7% over the past year and 0.6% in September alone, with gasoline up 9.1% in the month and diesel surging through freight costs into grocery and goods prices — cost pressure becoming the defining test two weeks before the midterm elections.
10. DailyBrief | At least four people were killed and 27 wounded in Russian missile and drone attacks on Ukraine's Kyiv region over the past day, Ukrainian officials said, following an energy-infrastructure barrage President Zelenskyy said left more than half a million people without electricity, heat and running water.
11. WSJ | President Trump cancelled plans to livestream the execution of the Fort Hood shooter, the Wall Street Journal reported — reversing a proposal Secretary Pete Hegseth had described as a deterrent that would have included execution by firing squad.
12. Gensler Research Institute | A three-part study of the 2026 FIFA World Cup by the Gensler Research Institute, ROAR and Oxford Economics found fans used collective language 70% more often when posting from the public spaces around stadiums than from inside them, rising 189% when posts carried awe — evidence the plazas, not just the venues, turn crowds into communities as sports districts draw a projected $100 billion-plus in global investment over 15 years.
13. Bonesville | A Brewers-Rays World Series matchup will produce a first-time champion — and possibly the first all-indoor World Series — a novelty finish to the baseball season whichever club wins.

## 2026-10-20 12:13 UTC
1. Sky at Night Magazine | Scientists say a temperature acting like a switch in the early universe offers a new explanation for how matter won out over antimatter after the Big Bang — a possible answer to why anything exists at all, with detectable imprints predicted on primordial gravitational waves, published in Physical Review Letters.
2. Medium | Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5, given plain-language descriptions of core quantum operations in a closed execution loop, discovered novel quantum circuit designs that beat state-of-the-art human benchmarks across eight domain primitives, in some cases cutting gate counts by more than an order of magnitude — AI now designing cheaper quantum software than humans.
3. Reuters | Russia has expanded strikes from eastern and central Ukraine to energy facilities in previously untargeted western regions including Lviv, Rivne, Ternopil and Khmelnytskyi, causing waves of blackouts ahead of winter, with DTEK saying an overnight attack hit three facilities in Odesa and left 32,700 families without electricity.
4. The Guardian | Tap water is no longer drinkable in Longyearbyen, Svalbard, after climate-related permafrost thaw exposed bedrock that is leaching heavy metals into the Isdammen lake that supplies the town — a concrete local collapse of a basic service driven by Arctic warming.
5. Reuters | Nvidia-backed Nscale is in talks to sell AI computing power to Anthropic in a second deal worth about $45 billion for another facility at its Monarch campus in West Virginia, delivering 460 megawatts using Nvidia Vera Rubin chips — a second mega-commitment on top of August's $45 billion deal as debt-driven AI infrastructure scrutiny sharpens.
6. NASA | NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory found the Treble Clef radio structure, extending over 2 million light-years, is likely caused by an outburst from a supermassive black hole followed by a collision of two galaxy clusters — a possible origin for one of the sky's strangest large-scale formations.
7. The Telegraph | Mainland Europe has recorded its highest ever number of West Nile virus cases, with 1,715 locally acquired cases so far this year compared with 989 at the same point last year according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, with Italy hardest hit — mosquito-borne disease expanding with warming conditions.
8. Reuters | The Kremlin said it hopes a meeting in Russia between President Putin and US special envoy Steve Witkoff can be organised in the near future, with Witkoff expected to brief Putin on Ukrainian and European positions after talks in Oslo with President Zelenskiy and the E4 — a possible direct Washington-Moscow follow-on channel.
9. CBC News | Alberta voters overwhelmingly backed remaining in Canada in the province's referendum, with about 76% for remain versus about 24% for beginning a process toward a separation vote in unofficial Elections Alberta results — a boost to Prime Minister Mark Carney's national-unity push amid the US trade war.
10. PERILS | Hailstorm Raphaela, the severe convective storms that hit France, Germany, Switzerland and Italy in late August, caused an insured loss of 3.296 billion euros, making it Europe's costliest convective storm event in PERILS records — extreme-weather losses setting a new European benchmark.
11. NPR | The 2026 US midterm elections are set to become the most expensive on record, with more than $15 billion raised to influence the outcome and control of Congress, NPR reported — campaign money reaching a new scale weeks before the vote.
12. Reuters | Battery-electric vehicle registrations in Europe rose 70.3% in September to around 30% market share, Reuters reported via Clean Energy Wire, as high oil prices, subsidies and more affordable models drove growth — the EV transition accelerating under energy-price pressure.
13. AIM News | Mozambique's government plans to invest about $235 million in adapting its health sector to climate change, a roadmap its health minister said aims to prevent an estimated 30,000 deaths and the loss of more than 1.6 million years of human life in one of the countries most vulnerable to cyclones, floods and heatwaves.
